text: Measures to create safe and healthy workplaces go beyond monetary costs.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: It is about ensuring that everyone is able to return home from work safe and healthy every day.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: I think this is the basic right of every worker.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Mr Louis Ng raised various issues outside the scope of the Bill amendment.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Nonetheless, I will address them as these touch on other provisions in the WSH Act.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: The vast majority of MOM's safety inspections are surprise inspections.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: For cases where we give early notice, it is to encourage self-rectification.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: In such cases, we do not provide the exact date and time.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: And even after the first inspection, we will follow up with surprise inspections to check that WSH practices are sustained by the company management and workers.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Our WSH inspectors do check on plans to manage workers' fatigue as well as on working hour violations.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: During MOM's inspections, we also ask workers to surface any salary deductions, including for the provision of safety equipment.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: It is part of our inspection procedures and regime to check if workers understand operating instructions.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Workers who face threats of unfair dismissal should approach MOM as soon as possible.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: We agree with Mr Louis Ng in partnering responsible civil society organisations to protect workers' welfare.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Civil society organisations can help to protect our workers by immediately reporting any cases of concern they have come across to MOM directly so that we can investigate and take companies to task if warranted.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Members have also raised other important issues, such as incentives for good WSH performance, greater focus on occupational diseases, workplace health and psychosocial issues, reporting by doctors, and introducing the use of more technology for WSH.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: WSHC already holds annual WSH awards to recognise companies and individuals with good WSH performance.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: We will consider if further incentives are needed to spur better WSH attainment.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: The total WSH (TWSH) movement initiated in 2014 has strengthened efforts to integrate safety with workplace health management, including occupational diseases and the psychosocial risk of workplace harassment.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: We have WSH Guidelines on Diagnosis and Management of Occupational Diseases.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: The tripartite partners will continue to work closely together to share learning and increase the awareness of occupational diseases in workplaces.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: MOM has also issued a Tripartite Advisory on Managing Workplace Harassment in 2015 which serves as a practical guide for employers on how to prevent workplace harassment, and for employees on where to seek help.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Under the WSH Act, it is already the duty of every employer to take, as far as is reasonably practicable, measures necessary not just to ensure the safety, but also the health of workers.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: For reporting, doctors can already submit an incident report directly to MOM online or in person.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: However, I would like to emphasise that the primary responsibility to report accidents should rightfully rest with the employer.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: We should not lessen this responsibility on the part of the employer.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: We will use more of such platforms to drive technology adoption to improve industry WSH practices.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Many of the Members' suggestions and ideas are excellent and will be discussed further with the tripartite and industry partners in the formulation of our WSH 2028 strategic plan.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: We believe that such close collaboration will enable us to reach our common goal of making all workplaces safer and healthier.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: For those Members where your points are not addressed today, rest assured that MOM will consider your ideas in our formulation of the WSH 2028 plan.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Once again, I thank Members of the House for their support of this Bill which will strengthen the culture of prevention in our workplaces.
